title: Elements
author: Euclid
text: Thirteen books that build geometry from a few definitions and five postulates. People learned mathematics from it for more than two thousand years.

title: The Compendious Book on Calculation by Completion and Balancing
author: Muhammad ibn Musa al-Khwarizmi
text: Its method of al-jabr — restoring a balance — gave algebra its name, and the author's own name became the word algorithm.

title: Book of Optics
author: Ibn al-Haytham
text: Argued that we see because light travels into the eye, and tested ideas about light with careful experiments rather than argument alone.

title: On the Revolutions of the Heavenly Spheres
author: Nicolaus Copernicus
text: Put the Sun, not the Earth, at the centre of the planets' orbits. Copernicus saw it printed in the year he died; the argument took another century to win.

title: On the Fabric of the Human Body
author: Andreas Vesalius
text: Published the same year as Copernicus. Vesalius drew what dissection actually showed, and corrected errors that had stood since Galen.

title: The Starry Messenger
author: Galileo Galilei
text: A small telescope pointed upward: mountains on the Moon, and four moons circling Jupiter.

title: Micrographia
author: Robert Hooke
text: Drawings made through a microscope — a flea the size of a page, and the little boxes in cork that Hooke named cells.

title: Principia
author: Isaac Newton
text: Three laws of motion and one of gravity: enough to explain a falling apple and the orbiting Moon with the same mathematics.

title: Species Plantarum
author: Carl Linnaeus
text: Gave every plant known to him a two-part name, genus then species — the naming system biologists still use.

title: Elementary Treatise of Chemistry
author: Antoine Lavoisier
text: Listed the chemical elements then known and showed that mass is conserved when substances react.

title: Notes on the Analytical Engine
author: Ada Lovelace
text: Notes on a mechanical computer that was never finished. They include what is often called the first published program, and the idea that such a machine could work on more than numbers.

title: On the Mode of Communication of Cholera
author: John Snow
text: Snow traced a cholera outbreak to a single water pump on Broad Street and argued that the disease spread through water, not foul air.

title: Notes on Matters Affecting the Health of the British Army
author: Florence Nightingale
text: Her diagrams showed that more soldiers in the Crimean War died of preventable disease than of their wounds.

title: On the Origin of Species
author: Charles Darwin
text: Evolution by natural selection, built from pigeons, barnacles, fossils and island birds. The first printing sold out to booksellers on the day it was issued.

title: Experiments on Plant Hybridization
author: Gregor Mendel
text: Years of crossing pea plants showed that traits pass on as separate units in predictable ratios. It was largely ignored until 1900.

title: Principles of Chemistry
author: Dmitri Mendeleev
text: Arranged the elements into a periodic table and left gaps for elements nobody had found yet — then predicted what they would be like.

title: A Treatise on Electricity and Magnetism
author: James Clerk Maxwell
text: Brought electricity, magnetism and light together under one set of equations.

title: Research on Radioactive Substances
author: Marie Curie
text: Marie Curie's doctoral thesis on radioactivity, completed in the same year she shared the Nobel Prize in Physics.

title: Periods of 25 Variable Stars in the Small Magellanic Cloud
author: Henrietta Swan Leavitt
text: Leavitt found that brighter Cepheid stars pulse more slowly — a ruler later used to measure the distances to other galaxies.

title: The Origin of Continents and Oceans
author: Alfred Wegener
text: Proposed that the continents drift. Rejected for decades, until evidence from the ocean floor arrived in the 1960s.

title: Stellar Atmospheres
author: Cecilia Payne
text: Payne's thesis showed that stars are made mostly of hydrogen and helium — against what almost everyone then believed.

title: On Computable Numbers
author: Alan Turing
text: Imagined a simple machine reading and writing symbols on a tape, and used it to define what can be computed at all.

title: Molecular Structure of Nucleic Acids
author: Watson, Crick — with Franklin and Gosling's X-ray evidence
text: The double helix, proposed in a one-page paper. Rosalind Franklin and Raymond Gosling's X-ray evidence appeared in the same issue of the journal.

title: Silent Spring
author: Rachel Carson
text: Showed how pesticides like DDT build up through food chains and harm wildlife, and helped start the modern environmental movement.
